title: MHFE specification main: targeted correctness and suite-3 implementation-conformance review

This is not a second full implementation audit, full bibliographic verification, formal proof or independent specialist cryptanalysis.

findings.title: Intermediate round salts are described as public although their disclosure enables a one-call password filter
findings.reproduction: Take the public zero-12 fixture. Give the attacker the container and additionally S_10 from its transcript. For each password candidate compute S_11 from the container left half, perform one real default-cost Argon2id evaluation with OpenSSL, reconstruct L_11, and compare the derived S_10 with the leaked value. Test the correct and one wrong password.
findings.expected: Distinguish a salt that does not have to be an independently stored secret from intermediate state-derived salt values that the ciphertext-only cost argument assumes are unavailable.
findings.observed: The README says salt derivation uses public data; the supplement calls state-derived salts not secret without limiting the statement to exposed endpoints. The actual extra-leak experiment accepted the correct password and rejected the wrong password using one Argon2id call each (6.72 and 6.86 seconds).
findings.impact: This is an inaccurate information-flow description with a concrete consequence for logging and diagnostics. It is NOT a ciphertext-only break: the experiment deliberately provides an extra intermediate salt. No production path leaking such a salt was discovered. The published-vector transcript is safe because its inputs are public. The cost claim needs its no-intermediate-leak premise stated explicitly.
findings.recommendedFix: State that the inverse endpoint salt S_11 is public from the container, S_0 is known when the original is known, and intermediate salts, masks, keys and states are transient sensitive values. Forbid their production logging/export and make the erasure recommendation explicitly include them. Distinguish this from the absence of a stored secret salt.
findings.requiredVerification: Review all ordinary-operation tracing and diagnostic paths; retain a public-fixture regression demonstrating the one-call filter and check that production interfaces expose no intermediate values. Correct both README and supplement. No suite/byte-format change is needed.

findings.title: Interactive CLI releases an unverified container into redirected stdout
findings.reproduction: Run the exact native CI binary with stdin attached to a PTY and stdout to a pipe, without --stdin. Enter the public zero-12 source and password twice. Read the pipe and stop the child as soon as the expected container is emitted.
findings.expected: A result passed to another program MUST NOT be released before reverse verification passes; eligibility for a human preview must depend on the output destination.
findings.observed: The expected container reached piped stdout after 73.74 seconds, before the Verified message and before reverse verification completed. The implementation selects the early-output branch solely from input.is_script(), while print_phrase writes stdout in both branches. The probe terminated the operation after observing the premature output.
findings.impact: A downstream program or redirected file can receive and act on a result whose verification later fails or never finishes. No corrupted fixture or actual loss was induced. This is a new implementation finding uncovered by normative conformance tracing, separate from the earlier incorrect rehearsal message.
findings.recommendedFix: Gate early presentation on a human output destination, or send only a clearly labelled preview to a terminal and reserve stdout for verified results. Handle stdin and stdout modes independently. Do not assume absence of --stdin means stdout belongs to a person.
findings.requiredVerification: Use a PTY/pipe matrix: terminal-to-terminal, terminal-to-pipe, script-to-terminal and script-to-pipe. Inject verification failure and cancellation after encryption; machine-facing stdout must contain no container unless verification succeeded.

findings.title: CLI line-based password transport cannot represent the full normative password domain
findings.reproduction: Pass alpha\nbeta and alpha\r as UTF-8 bytes to production WASM. Capture the normalized bytes at the engine boundary while deliberately stopping before Argon2. Supply the same intended newline-containing password twice to native encrypt --stdin using its documented line protocol.
findings.expected: Recovery MUST accept every password allowed by the fixed Unicode-17/NFKD/1..1024-byte rules. A recovery interface needs a lossless way to supply that domain, even if its convenient interactive field supports a subset.
findings.observed: WASM accepts LF, trailing CR, NUL and surrounding spaces and preserves their bytes. The repeated intended LF password is split into separate CLI answers and fails with exit 2 (passwords differ). read_line cannot embed LF in a field; strip_line_ending also removes a final CR before LF. The hidden terminal input is likewise line-oriented. There is no documented alternative password-byte transport in the CLI.
findings.impact: A valid container made through a byte-capable integration can be unrecoverable through the CLI interface even though the underlying Rust and WASM cryptographic password implementation is correct. This is an input-transport/interoperability gap, not a defect in NFKD or the permutation. The conformance-class ambiguity should also be clarified in the specification.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a lossless secret-input channel, for example a length-delimited stream, dedicated descriptor or explicitly encoded input format. Avoid secret command-line arguments. Document delimiter handling. Do not silently narrow suite-3 passwords: rejecting previously valid characters changes the frozen password definition and does not recover existing containers.
findings.requiredVerification: Cross-interface recovery for LF, CR, CRLF, NUL, tabs, leading/trailing spaces and normalization-equivalent inputs; verify byte preservation. The present test confirms normalization and transport failure, not a new full-cost container for every control character.

findings.title: README overstates what equal containers imply
findings.reproduction: Compare the unconditional equality statement in the README with the fixed-permutation qualifications in the supplement. Also consider two allowed source-length interpretations of one packed state.
findings.expected: Equality implies equality of packed state only when suite, normalized password, PIM and MEM identify the same permutation; equality of packed state is not always equality of source-length interpretation.
findings.observed: The README states that identical containers reveal the same phrase without those qualifications. The supplement correctly limits the converse to a fixed permutation and notes source-length ambiguity.
findings.impact: This is a precision and consistency defect, not a ciphertext collision attack. Across different passwords/settings, the same container generally decrypts to different states; one packed state can also have both a short-source and a 24-word interpretation.
findings.recommendedFix: Say that repeated encryption of the same packed source under the same normalized password, suite and settings is linkable. State the converse only for that same permutation and distinguish packed-state equality from source-length identity.
findings.requiredVerification: Check the statement against the permutation definition and the deliberate ambiguous-source fixture; keep README and supplement wording consistent.

recommendations.title: Separate conformance classes and strengthen final-output semantics
recommendations.recommendation: Define Core, CLI, Browser Client and Complete Application obligations. A core function cannot show a suite, ask twice or render warnings. Let an internal primitive return a typed UnverifiedContainer, but require a final container-export operation to complete reverse verification. Clarify how the SHOULD for verification interacts with the MUST NOT for machine output and the preview exception. This removes an ambiguity without changing ciphertext.

recommendations.title: Use explicit verification result types
recommendations.recommendation: Distinguish unchecked output, reverse_checked, short_verifier_match(words, bits), wallet_fingerprint_match and wallet_address_match. A generic verified=true is too easy to interpret as ownership or passphrase verification. Include the address derivation scope and say not_found_in_scope when a bounded search fails; a missing path match does not establish a wrong MHFE password.

recommendations.title: Publish a canonical suite-3 conformance corpus before stable release
recommendations.recommendation: Publish the 17 positive transcripts, negative vectors and Unicode boundary cases in mhfe-spec with immutable hashes and schema. Add LF/CR/CRLF, private-use and noncharacters; raw numerical API coercions belong in adapter tests. Keep production-cost known-answer tests separate from toy/reduced tests. Obtain another-author implementation: a second code path using independent OpenSSL is valuable but is not independent expert review.

recommendations.title: Keep performance claims conditional and add measured attacker scenarios
recommendations.recommendation: The arithmetic for 58 million years, 39 years and about 20.5 equivalent cost bits is consistent with the assumed 1 MHFE guess/s and 1.5 million PBKDF2 guesses/s. The rates are not benchmark results. Logical block accesses are not automatically DRAM traffic, and capacity, bandwidth and area-time models cannot be interchanged. Add exact hardware, optimized code, batching, password/salt reuse, memory-time trade-offs and sensitivity ranges; distinguish PBKDF2-only from complete address checking. Do not present the tables as a measured lower bound.

recommendations.title: Explain the parameter optimization objective explicitly
recommendations.recommendation: RFC 9106 recommends Argon2id t=1 at 2 GiB and notes t=1 is best for fixed defender time under its attacker model. Twelve passes are a valid project choice with a 2-GiB browser/memory ceiling, not the RFC preset and not established as globally optimal. Compare candidate memory/pass budgets empirically before a future suite. Do not reduce current suite-3 rounds or passes in place.

recommendations.title: Promote cumulative false-positive and reference-leak guidance to the short spec
recommendations.recommendation: For a selected 21-word verifier the per-uniform-candidate rate is 2^-32, but after q independent trials the chance of any false match is 1-(1-2^-32)^q. At one million trials this is about 0.0233%; at 2^32 trials about 63.2%. Auto detection is also dominated by the 21-word relation even for an intended 12-word source. Recommend selecting the known length during recovery assistance and confirming a wallet reference. These facts are mostly already in the supplement; promotion avoids overstating the word confirms. A no-passphrase master fingerprint can separately identify a mnemonic and remove the claimed pair-search advantage; document exactly what any saved reference derives from.

recommendations.title: Preserve recovery context as a portable offline package
recommendations.recommendation: State suite, supported implementation version, settings, wordlist, password encoding and reference path/network separately from the decoy plate, with an offline compatible release. Preserve access to suite-2 software. The current README reference link points to the repository root while suite3 exists on a WIP branch: pin the actual revision until release. No automatic suite guessing is safe for a 24-word source.

recommendations.title: Make historical suite-2 analysis unmistakably archival
recommendations.recommendation: Part II contains old PIM ranges and formulas lacking MEM alongside uppercase requirements, despite being non-normative. Replace the blanket read suite2 as current suite instruction with a precise applicability table or label every copied formula suite2. The current README is sufficient to implement suite3; the danger is copying the wrong historical formula.

recommendations.title: Keep entropy, passwords and recovery availability separate
recommendations.recommendation: The 256-bit state does not turn a 12-word source into 256 bits of entropy. Work factors do not repair correlated/reused passwords. The maximum joint MEM/PIM range is headroom: extrapolating the document own time model to 3 TiB and PIM1023 gives roughly 3-6 years per inversion, not a practical recommended profile. Publish realistic supported profiles and explicit resource/time ceilings without changing parameter mapping.

recommendations.title: Treat exact input matching and abort semantics as explicit adapter contracts
recommendations.recommendation: Specify raw versus normalized confirmation comparison (current CLI and client compare raw input bytes), ASCII word case handling, accepted whitespace, lossless binary/string transport and cancellation state. On cancellation after a preview, keep status unverified. Clarify that no copy/store during rehearsal prohibits external disclosure and persistence, not the transient internal representation required to derive a wallet.

limitations: No real-browser GUI/CSP/lifecycle testing, second clean build or other-OS execution in this follow-up.
No complete Unicode-17 normalization corpus or exhaustive protocol input domain. Fourteen accepted fixtures checked at the production WASM KDF boundary; invalid cases stop before it.

Fresh structural replay uses recorded Argon2 outputs and does not independently validate them. Two real full-cost OpenSSL evaluations were added only for the leaked-intermediate-salt experiment. Prior full-cost native/C-WASM/two-positive-vector evidence is inherited and explicitly identified.
No production intermediate-salt disclosure found. One-call filter assumes S_10 supplied as additional information; no claim of a one-call ciphertext-only attack.
Exact model/effort unknown. AUD-002 is locally assigned in the specification repository sequence and not reserved upstream; same textual IDs in mhfe repository denote different records.
No repairs, releases, pushes or remote mutations performed.
